#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Command-line wrapper around the JSON-backed notes core module.

The core storage logic lives in :mod:`notes` (the module produced by task 1,
"t1"); this file only parses arguments, calls that module, and prints results.

Usage
-----
::

    python cli.py add "buy milk"
    python cli.py list
    python cli.py delete 1

By default every command operates on ``notes.json`` in the *current working
directory*.  A different file can be selected with ``--file PATH`` placed
before the subcommand::

    python cli.py --file ~/notes.json list

Exit status is ``0`` on success and nonzero on any error (argparse uses ``2``
for malformed arguments, while storage/validation errors reported by the core
module use ``1``).  Only the Python standard library is used.

Note numbers are 1-based positions, so deleting a note renumbers the notes
that follow it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence

import notes

#: Name used in usage/error messages, regardless of how the script is invoked.
PROG = "cli.py"
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_ERROR = 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# subcommand handlers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _cmd_add(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Append one note (possibly several words joined by spaces)."""
    text = " ".join(args.text)
    number = notes.add_note(text, args.path)
    # The core module strips surrounding whitespace before storing.
    print(f"Added note #{number}: {text.strip()}")
    return EXIT_OK


def _cmd_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Print every note in numbered insertion order."""
    stored = notes.list_notes(args.path)
    if not stored:
        print("No notes yet.")
        return EXIT_OK
    for number, text in enumerate(stored, start=1):
        print(f"{number}. {text}")
    return EXIT_OK


def _cmd_delete(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Delete the note at the given 1-based number."""
    number = str(args.number).strip()
    removed = notes.delete_note(number, args.path)
    print(f"Deleted note #{number}: {removed}")
    return EXIT_OK


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# parser / entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Build the argparse parser with the ``add``/``list``/``delete`` commands."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog=PROG,
        description="Add, list, and delete notes stored in a JSON file.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-f",
        "--file",
        metavar="PATH",
        dest="path",
        default=notes.DEFAULT_PATH,
        help="notes file to use (default: %(default)s in the current directory)",
    )

    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(
        title="commands",
        dest="command",
        metavar="COMMAND",
        required=True,
    )

    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "add",
        help="append a new note",
        description="Append a new note to the notes file.",
    )
    add_parser.add_argument(
        "text",
        nargs="+",
        metavar="TEXT",
        help="note body; multiple words are joined with single spaces",
    )
    add_parser.set_defaults(func=_cmd_add)

    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "list",
        help="list all notes",
        description="Print all notes in numbered insertion order.",
    )
    list_parser.set_defaults(func=_cmd_list)

    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "delete",
        help="delete a note by its 1-based number",
        description="Delete the note at the given 1-based position.",
    )
    delete_parser.add_argument(
        "number",
        metavar="NUMBER",
        help="1-based number of the note to delete",
    )
    delete_parser.set_defaults(func=_cmd_delete)

    return parser


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run the CLI and return a process exit status.

    Argument-parsing failures raise :class:`SystemExit` (exit status ``2``) via
    argparse itself; storage and validation failures from the core module are
    reported on stderr and turned into exit status ``1``.
    """
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return args.func(args)
    except notes.NotesError as exc:
        # Covers NotesFileError, InvalidNoteNumber and NoteNotFoundError.
        print(f"{PROG}: error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_ERROR
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        # e.g. a blank note body rejected by notes.add_note.
        print(f"{PROG}: error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_ERROR


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover - exercised via subprocess test
    sys.exit(main())

"""Tests and smoke checks for the argparse CLI wrapper in cli.py."""

import ast
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import cli
import notes

CLI_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().with_name("cli.py")


@pytest.fixture()
def cwd(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Run the CLI from an empty temporary directory."""
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    return tmp_path


def run_cli(*argv):
    """Invoke cli.main() in-process and return its exit status."""
    return cli.main(list(argv))


def stored(cwd):
    """Read the canonical notes.json from the temporary CWD."""
    return json.loads((cwd / "notes.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# add
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_add_stores_note_via_core(cwd, capsys):
    assert run_cli("add", "some note") == 0
    assert "some note" in capsys.readouterr().out
    assert (cwd / "notes.json").exists()
    assert stored(cwd) == ["some note"]
    assert notes.list_notes(cwd / "notes.json") == ["some note"]


def test_add_joins_multiple_words(cwd):
    assert run_cli("add", "buy", "milk") == 0
    assert notes.list_notes(cwd / "notes.json") == ["buy milk"]


def test_add_reports_increasing_numbers(cwd, capsys):
    assert run_cli("add", "a") == 0
    assert run_cli("add", "b") == 0
    assert run_cli("add", "c") == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "#1" in out and "#2" in out and "#3" in out
    assert stored(cwd) == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_add_blank_note_is_an_error(cwd, capsys):
    assert run_cli("add", "   ") == 1
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "error" in err.lower()
    assert not (cwd / "notes.json").exists()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# list
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_list_empty_store(cwd, capsys):
    assert run_cli("list") == 0
    assert "No notes" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_list_prints_numbered_notes_in_order(cwd, capsys):
    run_cli("add", "first")
    run_cli("add", "second")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# end-to-end smoke check through a real subprocess

def test_subprocess_smoke(tmp_path):
    def run(*args):
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(CLI_PATH), *args],
            cwd=tmp_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )

    added = run("add", "some note")
    assert added.returncode == 0, added.stderr
    assert (tmp_path / "notes.json").exists()

    listed = run("list")
    assert listed.returncode == 0, listed.stderr
    assert "1. some note" in listed.stdout

    bad = run("delete", "9")
    assert bad.returncode != 0
    assert bad.stderr.strip()
    assert json.loads((tmp_path / "notes.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == [
        "some note"
    ]

    deleted = run("delete", "1")
    assert deleted.returncode == 0, deleted.stderr
    assert json.loads((tmp_path / "notes.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == []


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# standard-library-only constraint
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_cli_imports_only_stdlib_and_core_module():
    tree = ast.parse(CLI_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    imported = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            imported.update(alias.name.split(".")[0] for alias in node.names)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if node.level == 0 and node.module:
                imported.add(node.module.split(".")[0])

    allowed = set(sys.stdlib_module_names) | {"__future__", "notes"}
    assert imported <= allowed, f"non-stdlib imports: {sorted(imported - allowed)}"
